legge: Khien (represents) what is great and originating, penetrating, advantageous, correct and firm.
zing: Big energy. Total green light: you're the source, it all flows, and it pays off, as long as you stay real and stay firm. Full send.

legge: Khwan (represents) what is great and originating, penetrating, advantageous, correct and having the firmness of a mare. When the superior man (here intended) has to make any movement, if he take the initiative, he will go astray; if he follow, he will find his (proper) lord. The advantageousness will be seen in his getting friends in the south-west, and losing friends in the north-east. If he rest in correctness and firmness, there will be good fortune.
zing: Take the passenger seat. Grab the wheel and you'll wreck it; follow, and you'll find your person. Your people are southwest, your old crew's northeast. Stay steady and you're good.

legge: Kun (indicates that in the case which it presupposes) there will be great progress and success, and the advantage will come from being correct and firm. (But) any movement in advance should not be (lightly) undertaken. There will be advantage in appointing feudal princes.
zing: Day one is messy and that's normal. Big wins are coming if you stay on the right track, but don't rush. Find your squad.

legge: Mang (indicates that in the case which it presupposes) there will be progress and success. I do not (go and) seek the youthful and inexperienced, but he comes and seeks me. When he shows (the sincerity that marks) the first recourse to divination, I instruct him. If he apply a second and third time, that is troublesome; and I do not instruct the troublesome. There will be advantage in being firm and correct.
zing: I'm not chasing students. They come to me. Ask once, sincerely, and I'll teach you. Ask three times and I'm out. Stay on the straight and narrow.

legge: Hsu intimates that, with the sincerity which is declared in it, there will be brilliant success. With firmness there will be good fortune; and it will be advantageous to cross the great stream.
zing: Hold up. Trust the process, the payoff is real. Stay steady and even the big risky crossing works out.

legge: Sung intimates how, though there is sincerity in one’s contention, he will yet meet with opposition and obstruction; but if he cherish an apprehensive caution, there will be good fortune, while, if he must prosecute the contention to the (bitter) end, there will be evil. It will be advantageous to see the great man; it will not be advantageous to cross the great stream.
zing: You can be totally in the right and still hit a wall. Stay cautious and chill and it works out; fight it to the bitter end and it doesn't. Find a mentor. Don't take the big leap today.

legge: Sze indicates how, in the case which it supposes, with firmness and correctness, and (a leader of) age and experience, there will be good fortune and no error.
zing: Run it like a pro: discipline, integrity, and a leader who's actually been there. Then it's good, no fumbles.

legge: Pi indicates that (under the conditions which it supposes) there is good fortune. But let (the principal party intended in it) re-examine himself, (as if) by divination, whether his virtue be great, unintermitting, and firm. If it be so, there will be no error. Those who have not rest will then come to him; and with those who are (too) late in coming it will be ill.
zing: Great vibes with the right people, but check yourself first: are you consistent, are you real? If so, no problem. Early joiners are in; latecomers get left on read.

legge: Hsiao Khu indicates that (under its conditions) there will be progress and success. (We see) dense clouds, but no rain coming from our borders in the west.
zing: Clouds stacking up and no rain yet. It's coming, just not today. Keep making progress.

legge: (Li suggests the idea of) one treading on the tail of a tiger, which does not bite him. There will be progress and success.
zing: Walking up to a tiger and it doesn't bite. Bold move, good outcome. Stay respectful.

legge: In Thai (we see) the little gone and the great come. (It indicates that) there will be good fortune, with progress and success.
zing: Small stuff out, big stuff in. Peak flow. Good fortune all around.

legge: In Phi there is the want of good understanding between the (different classes of) men, and its indication is unfavourable to the firm and correct course of the superior man. We see in it the great gone and the little come.
zing: Nobody's on the same page. Wrong moment to push your principles loudly. The big is leaving, the small is arriving.

legge: Thung Zan (or ‘Union of men’) appears here (as we find it) in the (remote districts of the) country, indicating progress and success. It will be advantageous to cross the great stream. It will be advantageous to maintain the firm correctness of the superior man.
zing: Open invite. Meet people out in the open, not in a clique. Big goals work when you're together and you stay principled.

legge: Ta Yu indicates that, (under the circumstances which it implies), there will be great progress and success.
zing: Big win. Everything comes together. Huge success.

legge: Khien indicates progress and success. The superior man, (being humble as it implies), will have a (good) issue (to his undertakings).
zing: Stay humble and it works out. Low-key is high status, and it ends well.

legge: Yu indicates that, (in the state which it implies), feudal princes may be set up, and the hosts put in motion, with advantage.
zing: Everyone's hyped. Good time to start the plan and rally the crew. It works.

legge: Sui indicates that (under its conditions) there will be great progress and success. But it will be advantageous to be firm and correct. There will (then) be no error.
zing: Go with the flow, go big, stay legit. Roll with it and there's no regret.

legge: Ku indicates great progress and success (to him who deals properly with the condition represented by it). There will be advantage in (efforts like that of) crossing the great stream. (He should weigh well, however, the events of) three days before the turning point, and those (to be done) three days after it.
zing: Something's rotted. Fix it and it's a big win. Go for the big move, but plan for three days before and review three days after.

legge: Lin (indicates that under the conditions supposed in it) there will be great progress and success, while it will be advantageous to be firmly correct. In the eighth month there will be evil.
zing: Big momentum, so keep it real. But it won't last forever: in the eighth month, trouble. Don't coast.

legge: Kwan shows (how he whom it represents should be like) the worshipper who has washed his hands, but not (yet) presented his offerings;—with sincerity and an appearance of dignity (commanding reverent regard).
zing: Hands washed, offering not yet made: that held breath before the big moment. Be sincere, be dignified. People notice.

legge: Shih Ho indicates successful progress (in the condition of things which it supposes). It will be advantageous to use legal constraints.
zing: Something's stuck between your teeth. Time to bite through. Enforce the rules, fairly.

legge: Pi indicates that there should be free course (in what it denotes). There will be little advantage (however) if it be allowed to advance (and take the lead).
zing: Looking good is fine. Just don't let the aesthetic drive. Style over substance only gets you so far.

legge: Po indicates that (in the state which it symbolises) it will not be advantageous to make a movement in any direction whatever.
zing: It's coming apart. Not the day to start anything big. Sit tight.

legge: Fu indicates that there will be free course and progress (in what it denotes). (The subject of it) finds no one to distress him in his exits and entrances; friends come to him, and no error is committed. He will return and repeat his (proper) course. In seven days comes his return. There will be advantage in whatever direction movement is made.
zing: Comeback season. Nobody's blocking you, your people are showing up. It takes about a week. Go any direction you like.

legge: Wu Wang indicates great progress and success, while there will be advantage in being firm and correct. If (its subject and his action) be not correct, he will fall into errors, and it will not be advantageous for him to move in any direction.
zing: Be real. Great things if you're honest and unscripted. Fake it and it backfires. Don't make moves yet.

legge: Under the conditions of Ta Khu it will be advantageous to be firm and correct. (If its subject do not seek to) enjoy his revenues in his own family (without taking service at court), there will be good fortune. It will be advantageous for him to cross the great stream.
zing: Stay on the straight path. Don't just live off the family: get out there and work. Then take the big leap.

legge: I indicates that with firm correctness there will be good fortune (in what is denoted by it). We must look at what we are seeking to nourish, and by the exercise of our thoughts seek for the proper aliment.
zing: Watch what you feed yourself: food, people, thoughts. Choose what you take in on purpose.

legge: Ta Kwo suggests to us a beam that is weak. There will be advantage in moving (under its conditions) in any direction whatever; there will be success.
zing: The beam is bowing under the load. Too heavy. Make a move anyway, in any direction, and it works out.

legge: Khan, here repeated, shows the possession of sincerity, through which the mind is penetrating. Action (in accordance with this) will be of high value.
zing: Deep water, twice over. Your sincerity gets you through. Keep it honest, keep moving, it pays off.

legge: Li indicates that, (in regard to what it denotes), it will be advantageous to be firm and correct, and that thus there will be free course and success. Let (its subject) also nourish (a docility like that of) the cow, and there will be good fortune.
zing: Stay steady and correct and it flows. Keep a calm, cow-like energy and good things come.

legge: Hsien indicates that, (on the fulfilment of the conditions implied in it), there will be free course and success. Its advantageousness will depend on the being firm and correct, (as) in marrying a young lady. There will be good fortune.
zing: Mutual attraction. Be sincere and it goes well, like a good match. Good fortune.

legge: Hang indicates successful progress and no error (in what it denotes). But the advantage will come from being firm and correct; and movement in any direction whatever will be advantageous.
zing: Consistency wins. No mistakes if you stay the course. Go ahead, any direction.

legge: Thun indicates successful progress (in its circumstances). To a small extent it will (still) be advantageous to be firm and correct.
zing: Strategic retreat. That's not defeat. A little stubborn goodness still pays off.

legge: Ta Kwang indicates that (under the conditions which it symbolises) it will be advantageous to be firm and correct.
zing: You're strong. Use it right. Stay on the straight and narrow.

legge: In Zin we see a prince who secures the tranquillity (of the people) presented on that account with numerous horses (by the king), and three times in a day received at interviews.
zing: A prince gets rewards, a pile of horses, and three audiences in a day. Everyone's glad you showed up. Main character day.

legge: Ming I indicates that (in the circumstances which it denotes) it will be advantageous to realise the difficulty (of the position), and maintain firm correctness.
zing: The lights are dim. Be real about how hard it is, and stay steady. Dim your shine, keep your integrity.

legge: For (the realisation of what is taught in) Kia Zan, (or for the regulation of the family), what is most advantageous is that the wife be firm and correct.
zing: A home runs when the one holding it together stays steady and true.

legge: Khwei indicates that, (notwithstanding the condition of things which it denotes), in small matters there will (still) be good success.
zing: Everyone's at odds. Small stuff can still go well. Keep it small.

legge: In (the state indicated by) Kien advantage will be found in the south-west, and the contrary in the north-east. It will be advantageous (also) to meet with the great man. (In these circumstances), with firmness and correctness, there will be good fortune.
zing: Headwinds. Southwest is good, northeast isn't. Find a wise mentor, stay straight, and you'll be alright.

legge: In (the state indicated by) Kieh advantage will be found in the south-west. If no (further) operations be called for, there will be good fortune in coming back (to the old conditions). If some operations be called for, there will be good fortune in the early conducting of them.
zing: Relief is here. If there's nothing left to do, go home. If there's more to do, do it fast.

legge: In (what is denoted by) Sun, if there be sincerity (in him who employs it), there will be great good fortune:—freedom from error; firmness and correctness that can be maintained; and advantage in every movement that shall be made. In what shall this (sincerity in the exercise of Sun) be employed? (Even) in sacrifice two baskets of grain, (though there be nothing else), may be presented.
zing: Less is more, if you mean it. Even two bowls of grain make a proper offering. Don't flex; be sincere.

legge: Yi indicates that (in the state which it denotes) there will be advantage in every movement which shall be undertaken, that it will be advantageous (even) to cross the great stream.
zing: Gains all around. Any move works, even the risky crossing. Go big.

legge: Kwai requires (in him who would fulfil its meaning) the exhibition (of the culprit’s guilt) in the royal court, and a sincere and earnest appeal (for sympathy and support), with a consciousness of the peril (involved in cutting off the criminal). He should (also) make announcement in his own city, and show that it will not be well to have recourse at once to arms. (In this way) there will be advantage in whatever he shall go forward to.
zing: Call it out publicly, sincerely, and with a heads-up that it's risky. Don't rush to fight. Tell your home crowd first, then go for it.

legge: Kau shows a female who is bold and strong. It will not be good to marry (such) a female.
zing: Big, bold energy just walked in. Fun for a moment, but as a long-term commitment? No.

legge: In (the state denoted by) Zhui, the king will repair to his ancestral temple. It will be advantageous (also) to meet with the great man; and then there will be progress and success, though the advantage must come through firm correctness. The use of great victims will conduce to good fortune; and in whatever direction movement is made, it will be advantageous.
zing: Gather the crew. Show up at the family temple, meet the big mentor, bring a real offering. Any direction works.

legge: Shang indicates that (under its conditions) there will be great progress and success. Seeking by (the qualities implied in it) to meet with the great man, its subject need have no anxiety. Advance to the south will be fortunate.
zing: Rise slowly, big success. Meet someone high-level and don't stress. South's the vibe.

legge: In (the condition denoted by) Khwan there may (yet be) progress and success. For the firm and correct, the (really) great man, there will be good fortune. He will fall into no error. If he make speeches, his words cannot be made good.
zing: Boxed in, but there's still a way. Stay honest if you're the real deal. Don't talk it up; nobody's buying words right now.

legge: (Looking at) Zing, (we think of) how (the site of) a town may be changed, while (the fashion of) its wells undergoes no change. (The water of a well) never disappears and never receives (any great) increase, and those who come and those who go can draw and enjoy the benefit. If (the drawing) have nearly been accomplished, but, before the rope has quite reached the water, the bucket is broken, this is evil.
zing: Towns come and go but the well stays. Always there, always free. Don't break the bucket right before the water. Finish the pull.

legge: (What takes place as indicated by) Ko is believed in only after it has been accomplished. There will be great progress and success. Advantage will come from being firm and correct. (In that case) occasion for repentance will disappear.
zing: Nobody believes it until it's done. After it lands: big win. Stay straight and the regret fades.

legge: Ting gives the intimation of great progress and success.
zing: Big cooking. Massive success.

legge: Kan gives the intimation of ease and development. When (the time of) movement (which it indicates) comes, (the subject of the hexagram) will be found looking out with apprehension, and yet smiling and talking cheerfully. When the movement (like a crash of thunder) terrifies all within a hundred li, he will be (like the sincere worshipper) who is not (startled into) letting go his ladle and (cup of) sacrificial spirits.
zing: Thunder rolls and everyone shakes, but you laugh anyway. Keep your cool when the crash comes.

legge: When one’s resting is like that of the back, and he loses all consciousness of self; when he walks in his courtyard, and does not see any (of the persons) in it,—there will be no error.
zing: Stillness like a mountain at your back. Lose the ego, forget the crowd, no mistakes.

legge: Kien suggests to us the marriage of a young lady, and the good fortune (attending it). There will be advantage in being firm and correct.
zing: Slow courtship: gradual wins. Steady and honest, and it works.

legge: Kwei Mei indicates that (under the conditions which it denotes) action will be evil, and in no wise advantageous.
zing: Careful: moves right now go badly. Nothing here is a good deal.

legge: Fang intimates progress and development. When a king has reached the point (which the name denotes) there is no occasion to be anxious (through fear of a change). Let him be as the sun at noon.
zing: You're at the peak. Don't stress about it ending. Be like the sun at noon.

legge: Lu intimates that (in the condition which it denotes) there may be some little attainment and progress. If the stranger or traveller be firm and correct as he ought to be, there will be good fortune.
zing: Traveling light, small wins. Stay respectful and steady, and good luck follows.

legge: Sun intimates that (under the conditions which it denotes) there will be some little attainment and progress. There will be advantage in movement onward in whatever direction. It will be advantageous (also) to see the great man.
zing: Soft power. Small wins, go in any direction, and go see someone wise.

legge: Tui intimates that (under its conditions) there will be progress and attainment. (But) it will be advantageous to be firm and correct.
zing: Joy and good conversation. Great, just keep it real and steady.

legge: Hwan intimates that (under its conditions) there will be progress and success. The king goes to his ancestral temple; and it will be advantageous to cross the great stream. It will be advantageous to be firm and correct.
zing: Scatter and spread. Go to the temple, take the risky crossing, stay on the right path.

legge: Kieh intimates that (under its conditions) there will be progress and attainment. (But) if the regulations (which it prescribes) be severe and difficult, they cannot be permanent.
zing: Rules are great. Rules that suffocate don't last.

legge: Kung Fu (moves even) pigs and fish, and leads to good fortune. There will be advantage in crossing the great stream. There will be advantage in being firm and correct.
zing: Sincerity works even on pigs and fish. Good luck, take the leap, stay honest.

legge: Hsiao Kwo indicates that (in the circumstances which it implies) there will be progress and attainment. But it will be advantageous to be firm and correct. (What the name denotes) may be done in small affairs, but not in great affairs. (It is like) the notes that come down from a bird on the wing;—to descend is better than to ascend. There will (in this way) be great good fortune.
zing: Handle the small stuff, not the big stuff. Stay humble like a bird coming down to earth: down, not up.

legge: Ki Zi intimates progress and success in small matters. There will be advantage in being firm and correct. There has been good fortune in the beginning; there may be disorder in the end.
zing: Small things done; stay steady. Great start, messy ending. Don't coast.

legge: Wei Zi intimates progress and success (in the circumstances which it implies). (We see) a young fox that has nearly crossed (the stream), when its tail gets immersed. There will be no advantage in any way.
zing: The little fox almost makes it across, then its tail dips. Almost isn't done. Don't blow it at the finish, and don't take the leap just yet.
